anti_rules.instruction: Do not use past tense in the subject line (e.g., 'Fixed bug' or 'Added feature').
anti_rules.rationale: The imperative proxy rate is ~40%, and subjects consistently use imperative or descriptive present forms like 'fix', 'avoid', 'error out', 'deal with'.

anti_rules.instruction: Do not use generic subjects like 'Bug fix' or 'Update code' without specifying the subsystem or nature of the change.
anti_rules.rationale: Subjects are specific and descriptive, often with a subsystem prefix and a clear indication of what the commit does.

anti_rules.instruction: Do not write terse one-line bodies for non-trivial changes.
anti_rules.rationale: Non-trivial commits have substantial bodies (median ~990 characters) with thorough explanations.

anti_rules.instruction: Do not omit attribution trailers (Reported-by, Tested-by, etc.) when others contributed to identifying or validating the fix.
anti_rules.rationale: Torvalds consistently credits reporters, testers, and suggesters via trailers.

notes: The ~50% capitalization rate suggests no strict rule on capitalizing the first word of the subject; it depends on whether a prefix is present.
The imperative proxy rate of ~40% indicates Torvalds uses a mix of imperative ('fix', 'avoid') and descriptive ('deal with', 'error out early') forms, not strictly imperative.
About 38% of commits have no body at all, which includes merge commits and version tags—these are structurally different from authored patches.
The high Cc count (958) likely includes many merge commits where Cc trailers are inherited from the merged patches.
Sample size of 7 detailed commits limits confidence on some stylistic patterns; broader patterns inferred from aggregate statistics.

examples.good_body:
The atomisp_mrfld_power() function isn't actually ever called, because
the two call-sites have commented out the use because it breaks on some
platforms...

Rather than commenting out the use entirely, just disable it
semantically instead (using a "0 &&" construct)...

I really don't want my builds to have any warnings that can then hide
real issues.

Signed-off-by: Linus Torvalds <torvalds@linux-foundation.org>
examples.good_subject: atomisp: avoid warning about unused function
examples.why: Demonstrates lowercase prefix, concise subject, clear problem statement, rationale for the approach, and personal motivation. Includes Signed-off-by.

examples.good_body:
The lockdep asserts for the new follow_pfnmap() API "knows" that a
pfnmap always has a vma->vm_file...

So this codepath does actually need to check for vm_file being NULL.

Reported-by: Jann Horn <jannh@google.com>
Fixes: 6da8e9634bb7 ("mm: new follow_pfnmap API")
Cc: Peter Xu <peterx@redhat.com>
Signed-off-by: Linus Torvalds <torvalds@linux-foundation.org>
examples.good_subject: mm: fix follow_pfnmap API lockdep assert
examples.why: Shows proper use of subsystem prefix, imperative 'fix', concise explanation of the edge case, and complete trailers including Reported-by, Fixes, Cc, and Signed-off-by.

examples.good_body:
It turns out that udev under certain circumstances will concurrently try
to load the same modules over-and-over excessively...
examples.good_subject: module: error out early on concurrent load of the same module file
examples.why: Exemplifies a thorough, narrative-style body with extensive context, quotes from other developers, technical detail about the solution, caveats, and comprehensive trailers.

format.body: Multi-paragraph prose explaining the problem, context, rationale, and approach. May include quoted text from others, inline code references, and bracketed side notes. Separated from subject by a blank line.
format.subject: <optional-subsystem-prefix>: <lowercase imperative/descriptive summary>
format.trailers: Blank line before trailers. Common order: Link, Reported-by, Reported-and-tested-by, Fixes, Cc, Tested-by, Acked-by, Reviewed-by, Signed-off-by (author's Signed-off-by typically last).

rules.instruction: Use a lowercase subsystem prefix followed by a colon and space when the commit is scoped to a specific subsystem (e.g., 'mm:', 'x86:', 'vfs:').
rules.rationale: About 48% of subjects use a prefix, with common ones being 'mm', 'x86', 'tty', 'vfs', 'pipe', etc. The prefix is lowercase and followed by a colon.

rules.instruction: Keep the subject line concise, typically under 72 characters, with a median around 44 characters.
rules.rationale: The median subject length is 44 characters and the mean is ~39 characters, indicating a preference for brevity.

rules.instruction: Write the body as a narrative explanation of the problem, the reasoning behind the fix, and the approach taken, using natural prose paragraphs.
rules.rationale: Bodies are typically multi-paragraph prose (median 5 paragraphs) that explain context, root cause, and rationale in a conversational but technical style.

rules.instruction: Always include a 'Signed-off-by' trailer with the author's name and email.
rules.rationale: 69% of commits include Signed-off-by, and virtually all commits with a body include it. It is the standard sign-off for kernel commits.

rules.instruction: Include 'Cc:' trailers to notify relevant maintainers and developers.
rules.rationale: Cc is the most common trailer (958 occurrences across 1000 commits), used extensively to notify stakeholders.

rules.instruction: Include 'Reported-by:' and 'Fixes:' trailers when the commit addresses a reported bug or regression.
rules.rationale: Reported-by appears 234 times and Fixes 176 times, indicating consistent attribution of bug reporters and linking to the offending commit.

rules.instruction: Do not capitalize the first word after a subsystem prefix (use lowercase for the description part).
rules.rationale: When a prefix is present, the word after the colon is typically lowercase (e.g., 'mm: fix', 'module: error out', 'atomisp: avoid').

rules.instruction: Omit the body for trivial or version-bump commits (e.g., release tags).
rules.rationale: About 38% of commits have no body, and version tag commits like 'Linux 6.9' and 'Linux 5.10-rc6' have empty bodies and no trailers.

rules.instruction: Explain the 'why' thoroughly in the body, not just the 'what', including background context and side effects.
rules.rationale: Torvalds' commit bodies frequently include extensive rationale, quoting others, explaining edge cases, and noting caveats. The rationale_rate is 37.8%.

rules.instruction: Use bracketed side notes (e.g., '[ Side note: ... ]') for tangential but relevant information.
rules.rationale: Torvalds uses square-bracket asides within commit bodies to add supplementary context without disrupting the main narrative flow.

rules.instruction: Do not end the subject line with a period.
rules.rationale: None of the sample subjects end with a period, consistent with standard kernel commit style.

avoid: Leaving out the 'why' behind a change
do: Explain the root cause and reasoning in detail
Use conversational but technically precise language
Quote relevant context from mailing list discussions
Mention caveats, edge cases, and limitations explicitly
Use emphatic language when something is important (e.g., 'horribly horribly wrong')
Include concrete data and measurements when available
tone.summary: Direct, technically precise, conversational, and opinionated. Explains reasoning thoroughly with a confident, sometimes blunt voice. Not afraid to editorialize or express frustration with bad patterns.
